prompt: The muscular wall of the heart's left ventricle is much thicker than that of the right ventricle. Why?

options.text: The left ventricle holds more blood because it is simply a bigger chamber in every dimension
The right ventricle does no pumping, so it needs no thick wall
The left ventricle must pump blood at higher pressure around the whole body, while the right ventricle only pumps it the short distance to the lungs
The left ventricle pumps blood uphill and the right pumps it downhill

explanation: The systemic circuit to the whole body offers far more resistance than the short pulmonary circuit to the lungs, so the left ventricle needs a thicker, stronger wall to generate the higher pressure required.
